svg.title: Component · Blended clip row · not-available · wide
svg.desc: Mirrors App/BlendedClipRow.swift for a clip whose file is neither on this device nor on PicPlace (2026-09-26, plan §15 — "A clip that is not here claims only what PicPlace holds" — and §16): PicPlace's list for the project has been read and does not name the file, or PicPlace holds none of the project's heavy files (PicPlaceController.blendAvailability == .notOnPicPlace). It happens to a blend that was only ever on the device that made it — Victory Bridge Sunset on the 18 Pro, whose six rows used to say On PicPlace and offer a Download that failed four times. The row keeps the blend's still (posters/<blend id>.jpg rides the records bundle even when the clip never went up) with components/holdings-pill.blend.nowhere.svg at 0.8, 2 pt in — the slashed layers alone (square.3.layers.3d.slash), no cloud: PicPlace holds none of it. The subtitle leads with "Not available to download · " (BlendWhereLine), and there is no button: BlendDownloadButton draws nothing unless the list holds the file, so the text column runs to the row's Spacer (x 335 — HStack spacing 12 before it, 14 padding). While the list is still unread (.unknown) the row claims neither way: the plain subtitle, no button, and holdings-pill.blend.there (grey layers, no cloud). A tap on the row still asks (the parent's onPlay → .fetchPrompt), and the prompt can only say the clip isn't on PicPlace (FetchOffer.notUploaded / .unavailable). The words are interim — Steven's copy pass (docs/TODO.md).

g.text: Not available to download · 24 fps · yesterday
